rules.rule: A tuple constructor analyzed as a static list gives an expression for each element, in order, and none for an empty tuple or a trailing comma
Static list elements are returned without interpretation, so they can be analyzed in turn, as static traversals or static lists

Static list analysis of any expression other than a tuple constructor is an error, even when its value is a tuple: a for expression, a variable, the keyword null, a template, a conditional, an index or splat on a tuple constructor, or an object constructor
A tuple constructor in parentheses is not a static list, so the analysis is an error (disputed)
An object constructor analyzed as a static map gives a key and a value expression for each element, in source order, whether separated by = or :, and none for an empty object or a trailing comma
A static map keeps every element, including elements with equal keys, instead of letting the later one replace the earlier

A static map key is the value of its key expression, not converted to a string, so it can be a number, a tuple, a parenthesized bool, null or unknown value, or the unwrapped value of a template with a single interpolation
A static map key expression follows the object constructor's key rules: a bare identifier gives its name as a string, a quoted key its text, and a parenthesized key the value of the expression inside
A bare true, false or null key gives the string of its name in a static map (disputed)
Evaluating a static map key that is a bare traversal of more than one step is an evaluation error (disputed)

Static map values are returned without interpretation, so they can be analyzed in turn, as static calls or static traversals, and a key written as a bare traversal of more than one step can be analyzed as a static traversal, on its own or together with the values
A bare identifier key, or a bare true, false or null key, analyzed as a static traversal is a root of its name, although evaluating the same key gives its name as a string (disputed)
A static map key analyzed as a static call, static list or static map is an error, even when the key is written in that syntax (disputed)

Static map analysis of any expression other than an object constructor is an error, even when its value is an object: a for expression, a variable, the keyword null, a tuple constructor, a template, or an attribute access on an object constructor
An object constructor in parentheses is not a static map, so the analysis is an error (disputed)
A function call analyzed as a static call gives the function's name and an expression for each argument, in order, and none for an empty argument list or a trailing comma
A static call's name is the function name exactly as written, including dashes, non-ASCII letters and combining marks, which aren't normalized, and no function of that name needs to exist
Static call arguments are returned without interpretation, so they can be analyzed in turn, as static traversals or static calls
A static call gives a final argument expanded with ... like any other argument, without the expansion, even when the argument isn't a list or tuple (disputed)
A static call of a namespaced function gives the name joined with ::, however many levels it has (disputed)
A static call of a function named true gives the name true (disputed)

Static call analysis of any expression other than a function call is an error: a variable, the keyword null, a quoted string, a template, an operation on a call, or an attribute access or index on a call's result
A function call in parentheses is not a static call, so the analysis is an error (disputed)
A variable analyzed as a static traversal gives a traversal rooted at its name exactly as written, including dashes and combining marks, which aren't normalized, whether or not the variable exists
Each attribute access after the root gives an attribute step with its name exactly as written, including a keyword or a combining mark, in source order among the other steps

Each index operation whose key is a literal gives an index step with the key's value: a number, including a non-integer, true, null, or a string written as a quoted string, including an empty one and one with escapes, or as a heredoc, which stays an index step rather than an attribute step
A legacy index such as .0 gives an index step with the number, not an attribute step
The keywords true, false and null analyzed as static traversals are roots of those names, which can be followed by steps
An index whose key refers to a variable isn't constant, so a traversal with it is not a static traversal
An index whose key is a constant expression other than a literal, such as -1, 1 + 1, (0) or a template with an interpolation, is not a static traversal step, so the analysis is an error (disputed)
A splat is neither an attribute access nor an index operation, so a traversal with a full or attribute-only splat is not a static traversal

Static traversal analysis of an expression that isn't a variable or one of the keywords true, false and null, with or without steps after it, is an error: a number, a quoted string, a template, a function call or an attribute of its result, an indexed tuple constructor or an operation
A traversal in parentheses, steps after a parenthesized variable, and a parenthesized object key are not static traversals, so the analysis is an error (disputed)

Static analysis doesn't evaluate the analyzed expression, so it succeeds in literal-only mode, where evaluating a variable or a function call is an error, and a static call doesn't call the function, even one that would fail

The expressions a static analysis gives are evaluated like any other expression, so an undefined variable in an element, key, value or argument, or a variable argument in literal-only mode, is an evaluation error rather than an analysis error
When a list element, map key or value, or call argument fails the analysis given for it, the whole analysis fails, even when the other parts succeed
An optional attribute with an analysis that the body doesn't define has nothing to analyze, so it is absent without an error
An attribute can be analyzed wherever it is defined, including in a block body and in the body partial processing leaves
